text:
maria-finance: Quick FYI — we've updated vendor approval thresholds and virtual card guidance effective immediately. Please read and apply for any in-flight requests. https://redwood.company/finance/procurement-updates :mega:

procurement-bot: NEW POLICY POSTED by @maria-finance
- Vendors <$5k: team-level approval (use virtual card)
- Vendors $5k–$50k: finance manager approval + PO required
- Vendors >$50k: legal + procurement + finance director sign-off
- Personal subscriptions: never charged to company card without pre-approval (reminder)

maria-finance: tl;dr — small purchases move faster, but anything over $5k needs a PO and will take longer. Use `#finance-vcards` to request a virtual card for one-off spend. :card_file_box:

sam-engineering: quick question — is open-source vendor hosting included? e.g., a $7k annual plan from a repo-hosted CI provider

lina-ops: @sam-engineering if it's a paid vendor providing SaaS to the company, treat as regular vendor. $7k -> PO required, start procurement workflow.

sam-engineering: ok thanks. Do we have a template PO description to paste?

maria-finance: yes — use the PO template under the doc linked above. Example snippet to copy into the PR description:

```
Project: Mobile Push Infra
Vendor: FastCI Inc.
Amount: $7,000/year
Business justification: Required for CI parallelism to meet SLOs and reduce build time by ~40%.
Contract term: 12 months
Contact: infra@redwood.com
```

procurement-bot: Reminder: submit the request using `/procure create` and attach vendor W9 or equivalent. Missing docs will delay approvals.

ceo-adam: Appreciate the clear thresholds. Two requests for leadership: 1) please add an escalation path for time-sensitive purchases under $20k if engineering has exec sign-off; 2) finance — consider a self-serve exception form for recurring SaaS so central ops doesn't block velocity.

maria-finance: noted. We'll add an escalation checkbox on the request form for purchases < $20k with a required exec note. Also evaluating a recurring SaaS fast-track for approved vendors.

sam-engineering: pinging to confirm turnaround targets? Curious how long approvals take at each tier.

maria-finance: estimated SLA: team-level < 48 hours, $5k–$50k ~ 3–5 business days, > $50k depends on negotiation (~2–3 weeks). Exceptions: emergency purchases can be escalated (use `#finance-escalations`).

lina-ops: FYI ops will maintain an "approved vendors" list to speed renewals. If you rely on a vendor a lot, flag them in the request so we can onboard proactively.

sam-engineering: great, will do. thanks! :thumbsup:

maria-finance: final note — image of cost center mapping is in the doc. Use `GL` codes when creating POs, e.g., `GL-4001` for infra, `GL-4203` for marketing. If unsure, put `GL-9999` and finance will reassign.

procurement-bot: policy version: 2026-03-23_v2.0 — archived old version at https://redwood.company/finance/procurement-archive

maria-finance: I'll run a short walk-through in next week's all-hands for new hires and folks who process purchases. If you have edge cases, drop them in this thread or DM me.

sam-engineering: appreciated.

lina-ops: +1 — sharing with ops channels now.
